statusText: The CME weekend halt continues to govern the assessment: no venue has quoted NQ since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and none will until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about twelve hours beyond the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail therefore holds at 10% (low), keeping the action EA_ON and the status green - a pathological one-way price path cannot form while nothing is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than observed extension. The wires moved again in the last hour, on the front that matters most for transmission: an ADNOC tanker was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz at roughly 09:54 UTC, the third such vessel strike in under a week and the fourth distinct escalation of this Saturday session after two earlier vessel attacks near 07:22 UTC, the Houthi ballistic-missile barrage on Mokha near 08:45 UTC and the IDF strikes in the Nabatieh area near 08:08 UTC. No injuries were reported in the latest attack. Stress firms one point to 52% (elevated) to carry that accumulation. It does not firm further, because the cross-asset evidence remains genuinely split: VIX closed Friday at 14.25, less than a point above its 52-week low of 13.38, and the Nasdaq-100 closed down only 0.13% and roughly 2.3% below its 52-week high. Confidence is 60% (solid) - every non-price dimension was re-verified this hour from primary sources and the readings are mutually consistent, while the price evidence is stale by necessity rather than by omission.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (10%) alone. No venue quotes NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint sits just beyond the horizon at the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, and the danger window brackets that reopen together with its first 90 minutes of price discovery - a full weekend of accumulated headlines expresses there as an opening gap, not as intraday structure. Gap risk remains genuinely two-way. Pulling one way: a Hormuz closure Tehran ties to conditions Washington has not met, a third ADNOC vessel strike in under a week with fifteen such vessels hit cumulatively, an IEA warning that global stockpile drawdown makes reopening more pressing, WTI at $82.40 after a +5% week and +33% year, and a 10Y at 4.70% pressing a 19-month high on long-end inflation aversion. Pulling the other: Iran and Oman are reported close to a waterway-management deal, VIX sits near its 52-week low, and Friday's tape absorbed both the escalation and a soft data print with a mid-range settle rather than a liquidation. Treat the reopen as a checkpoint to be scored on observed price path, not as a pre-committed direction.
headline: A third Hormuz tanker strike in a week lands at 09:54 UTC with no tape to price it - Tail holds at 10% on EA_ON while Stress firms to 52% against a VIX still near its 52-week low.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from primary quote sources, remains benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, with the session settling mid-range inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide, and no close near either extreme. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range and about 2.3% below the 52-week high of 30,762.20; NQ itself sits about 2.7% below its own 52-week high of 30,975.50. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle, at a level several percent off the highs, is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension and pinning near extremes that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency is not merely low - it is unmeasurable, because nothing has traded for more than thirteen hours.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close). The evidence is split, which is the central fact of this assessment. Equity volatility is calm to the point of complacency: VIX closed at 14.25, down 0.38 or 2.60% on the day, inside a 14.18-14.72 range, and only 0.87 points above its 52-week low of 13.38 against a 52-week high of 35.30. Rates and energy tell the opposite story. The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 5bp Friday to 4.70%, approaching the 19-month high of 4.75% set earlier in the week, on renewed long-end aversion tied to inflation concerns; the 2-year rose about 3bp to 4.18%, leaving the curve steepening rather than signalling a growth scare, with the effective fed funds rate steady at 3.63%. The Federal Reserve H.15 release confirms the trajectory into Friday, with the 2-year at 4.15% and the 10-year at 4.63% on 13 August. WTI settled at $82.40, +1.42% on the day, +5% on the week and +32.95% on the year; Brent at $88.52, +1.67% on the day and +34.43% on the year. Sector-level weakness on Friday was concentrated in semiconductors rather than broad, and the Nasdaq still closed a third consecutive higher week.

GEOPOLITICS (observed, and the only thing that moved this hour). The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed since fighting began in late February. In the last hour an ADNOC tanker was attacked while transiting the strait at roughly 09:54 UTC with no injuries reported - the third such incident in under a week, following two vessels struck earlier this morning near 07:22 UTC. Cumulatively fifteen ADNOC vessels have been hit, with one crew member killed and twenty injured. Elsewhere this session, Houthi forces fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mokha near 08:45 UTC, killing a security guard, wounding eight and leaving two marines missing, and the IDF confirmed strikes on Hezbollah targets in the Nabatieh area including Ansar, where seven were killed. Iran and Oman are reported close to a deal on managing the waterway, but the IRGC has reiterated that reopening depends on Washington accepting Iran's conditions, ending the war and withdrawing troops. The IEA has warned that reopening is becoming more pressing as global stockpiles draw down.

ASSESSMENT. Tail is held at 10% and stays deep in the low band. Every element the definition asks for - persistent directional efficiency, failed retracements, repeated extension, NQ holding near extremes - is either absent in the last observed session or unobservable in a halted market, and the non-zero level exists to price weekend headline discontinuity that must eventually clear through a gap. That maps to EA_ON and green. Stress firms one point to 52% (elevated). The accumulation is real: a fourth distinct escalation today, a third vessel strike in a week, oil up 5% on the week with a stockpile warning attached, and a 10-year pressing a 19-month high. It is held to one point because the counter-evidence is equally observed and equally fresh - a VIX within a point of its 52-week low and an index down 0.13% do not describe a market braced for a difficult high-volatility environment, and the contract is explicit that conflicting signals should raise Stress rather than Tail. dominantMode is mixed for exactly that reason. Confidence is 60% (solid): NQ futures, the NDX cash index, VIX, both key Treasury maturities via two independent sources, WTI and Brent, the geopolitical wire and the seven-day U.S. calendar were each read directly from primary or exchange-quote sources this hour and agree with one another. The ceiling on confidence is the structural absence of a live price path - a limitation no provider can escape this weekend - not a gap in what was gathered.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-10% throughout, so the action was EA_ON and the status green in every available slot. Tail held 8-9% across Friday's U.S. cash session as the data landed and produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, then printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress traced a clear event arc: 28-38% through the Friday morning hours, building to 40-44% across the U.S. cash session, then easing to 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. From 06:00 UTC the weekend escalation sequence lifted the series steadily - Tail to 10% and Stress through 48%, 50% and 51% - as the Mokha barrage, the Nabatieh strikes and the morning vessel attacks landed one after another with no tape to absorb them. Confidence ran 30-59%, weakest in Friday's pre-data European hours and settling at 59% across the weekend halt. The 20:00 UTC slot on 14 August is unavailable because no successful Claude snapshot was published for that hour; those fields are null and no past opinion has been rewritten.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 10:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 09:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly twelve hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is projected flat at 10% through the Saturday slots, ticking to 11% from 20:00 UTC as the reopen edges into view and to 12% in the final two Sunday-morning slots; those increments reflect accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to hold at 52% through the European afternoon, ease a single point to 51% across the thin Saturday U.S. hours when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, then firm back to 52% from 20:00 UTC and to 53-54% through Sunday's European morning as unresolved threads converge on the reopen. Confidence drifts from 60% to 57% across the horizon as the last live prints age further without replacement. The material catalyst sits just beyond the horizon: the CME reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery, which the danger window brackets. Inside the horizon the realistic risks are headline-driven - a further Hormuz vessel strike, a breakdown or breakthrough in the Iran-Oman waterway talks, or a U.S.-Iran development over the weekend - each of which would move Stress and the expected gap rather than produce observable one-way structure. The first genuine scheduled checkpoint is Monday's Empire State print at 12:30 UTC, and the week's highest-impact item is the FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday 19 August.
